drivers.name: Atlona AT-OME-MS Series Matrix Switcher
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls the Atlona AT-OME-MS family of 4K/UHD matrix presentation switchers (MS42 / MS42-HDBT / MS52 / MS52W / MS52W-EU) over Telnet on TCP port 23. Routes any of five inputs (USB-C / DisplayPort / HDMI / HDMI / BYOD) to two outputs (HDBaseT and HDMI), with audio volume / mute (HDMI and analog independently), CEC display control, USB host switching, and per-input signal detection. Use this driver for the Display:Matrix:Set protocol family; the older PS62 with its xNAVxM syntax is covered by atlona_ome_ps62.

help.overview: AT-OME-MS matrices route HDMI / DisplayPort / USB-C sources to a HDBaseT extender output and a local HDMI output. Audio is independent of video routing — the HDMI and analog outputs each have their own mute and a shared system volume in dB. Display power can be controlled over CEC. USB host follow modes let a connected control host follow the active video source.
help.setup:
1. Set a static IP on the matrix via its web UI (or DHCP reservation).
2. If Telnet Login Mode is ON in the matrix's web UI (System tab), enter the same Username and Password used for the web GUI in this driver's config. Leave both blank if Telnet Login Mode is OFF.
3. Atlona requires at least 500 ms between commands; the driver enforces that automatically.
4. Use Set Matrix Mode to switch between single-input (both outputs follow Display:Input:Set) and matrix mode (per-output routing via Display:Matrix:Set).

compatible_models.notes: All MS-series presentation matrices share the dotted Display:Matrix:Set / Audio:Volume:Set command vocabulary. MS42 (4x2) inputs 0-3, MS52/MS52W (5x2) inputs 0-4. The MS52W adds a 4 = BYOD wireless-link input. Outputs are always 0=HDBaseT, 1=HDMI. The driver advertises the 0-4 input range; the device rejects anything it doesn't have.

drivers.name: Atlona AT-OME-PS62 Matrix Switcher
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls the Atlona AT-OME-PS62 6x2 4K/UHD matrix presentation switcher over Telnet on port 23. Routes any of six inputs (HDMI / USB-C / HDBaseT) to two outputs (HDBaseT and HDMI). Independent four-zone audio with per-zone volume and mute, analog audio source routing, USB host switching, front-panel lock, and identify (POWER LED blink).

help.overview: The PS62 routes six HDMI / USB-C / HDBaseT sources to a HDBaseT and a HDMI output. Audio is independent: each of the two video outputs and two analog audio outputs has its own volume and mute. Analog audio can follow the HDBaseT or HDMI feed, or pull from one of three auxiliary inputs.
help.setup:
1. Set a static IP on the matrix via its web UI (or DHCP reservation). 2. If Telnet Login Mode is ON in the matrix's web UI, enter the same
   Username / Password used for the web GUI in this driver's config.
   Leave both blank if Telnet Login Mode is OFF.
3. Atlona requires a 500 ms minimum delay between commands; the driver
   is pre-configured for this.

compatible_models.notes: 6x2 4K/UHD matrix presentation switcher with USB hub. The MS42 / MS52 / MS52W family in the OME line uses a completely different command syntax (Display:Matrix:Set...) and is covered by a separate driver.

drivers.name: Atlona AT-UHD-PRO3 Matrix
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls the Atlona AT-UHD-PRO3 series of HDBaseT matrix switchers (PRO3-44M / 66M / 88M / 1616M) via Telnet on port 23. Supports source routing (per output, all outputs, multi-output), per-output volume and mute, power, presets (save / recall / clear), front-panel lock, and identify. State is mirrored for outputs 1-10 (covers 88M fully; 1616M outputs 11-18 are routable but not state-mirrored).

help.overview: Atlona PRO3 matrices route HDMI sources to HDBaseT extender outputs over a Cat5e/6 link to remote receivers. Use the Route command to send a source to a specific output, the Route to All command to send one source everywhere, and per-output volume / mute for HDBaseT zone audio. Save up to 50 routing presets.
help.setup:
1. Set a static IP on the matrix via its web UI (or DHCP reservation). 2. If IPLogin is enabled (factory default), enter the Username and
   Password configured on the matrix in this driver's config — the
   driver handles the "Login:" / "Password:" handshake automatically.
   Leave both blank if you've turned IPLogin off (per KB01392).
3. Atlona requires a 500 ms minimum delay between commands; the
   driver sends commands at that rate by default.
4. To activate a routing preset from a macro: configure the routing
   you want via individual Route commands, then send the Save Preset
   command with a preset number. Recall later with Recall Preset.

compatible_models.notes: AT-UHD-PRO3 series HDMI-to-HDBaseT matrix switchers. Output ranges vary by model (44M: 1-4, 66M: 1-6, 88M: 1-7+9 HDBaseT plus 8/10 HDMI mirrors, 1616M: 1-16+ mirrors). Driver state mirrors outputs 1-10. Larger 1616M outputs (11-18) accept routing commands but don't update state. Send a "Mreset" or "All#" to recover from surprising routing if a manual front-panel change happens.

drivers.name: Atlona OmniStream
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Atlona OmniStream Pro, R-Type, and Wallplate AV-over-IP encoders and decoders via the Telnet CLI (port 23). Supports source routing, audio mute/volume, video enable, HDCP, analog speaker power, and CEC/RS-232 display triggers. Runtime control surface only — install-time setup is configured in the device's web UI.

help.overview: Atlona OmniStream is an AV-over-IP encoder/decoder system. Encoders take HDMI sources and produce network streams; decoders pick a stream and output HDMI to a display. Routing happens by setting which IP stream each decoder receives (the VideoInput command).
help.setup:
1. Set a static IP on the OmniStream unit via its web UI. 2. If Telnet login authentication (IPLogin) is enabled on the device,
   enter the unit's Username and Password in this driver's config —
   the driver will handle the "Login:" / "Password:" handshake. Leave
   both blank if IPLogin is disabled.
3. Configure encoder sessions (multicast addresses, video format)
   and decoder IP inputs in the web UI before driver use.
4. Connect this driver to port 23. The HDMI output index ranges
   1..2 on most decoders; the session index ranges 1..6.
5. Volume range is 0..15 (Atlona's native scale). 6. To route a source: send the "Set Video Input" command with the
   output number and the IP input name (e.g. "ip_input3") configured
   on the decoder's web UI.

compatible_models.notes: All OmniStream Pro, R-Type, and Wallplate models on firmware 2.0+. Some audio commands (mute, volume, AudioInput, AnalogPower, DisplayBtn, VolumeBtn, InputBtn) are Pro-only and silently no-op on R-Type units.

drivers.name: Blackmagic Videohub
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Blackmagic Design Videohub routers over the Videohub Ethernet Protocol (TCP 9990). Supports video output routing, monitoring output routing, input/output label editing, and output locking across the entire Videohub product line.

help.overview: Blackmagic Videohub is a family of SDI matrix routers used in broadcast, post-production, and live event facilities. This driver speaks the Videohub Ethernet Protocol, used by every Videohub server-class device since 2010. It exposes video routing, monitoring routing, lock state, and label editing as macro-callable commands.
help.setup:
1. Connect the Videohub to your network via Ethernet.
2. Find the unit's IP address from the front panel (Smart Videohub) or from Blackmagic Videohub Setup.
3. The Videohub Ethernet Protocol on TCP 9990 is always enabled — no auth, no enable step.
4. Enter the IP address in the device config; leave port at 9990.
5. Outputs and inputs are 1-indexed in commands.
6. Routing 'output X to input Y' sends VIDEO OUTPUT ROUTING with the protocol's 0-indexed values.

compatible_models.notes: Confirmed against real hardware (firmware 9.0) via a community test report: video routing, input/output labels, output locks, and unsolicited state updates all work. This model has no monitoring outputs, so monitoring routing does not apply to it.

All current Videohub products share the v2.3 Ethernet Protocol. Pre-declared state variables cover the first 16 video ports + 4 monitoring outputs; routing on wider frames still works, additional ports surface as raw keys.

drivers.name: Extron SIS Protocol
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Extron products via the SIS (Simple Instruction Set) protocol. Covers crosspoint matrix switchers (DXP, CrossPoint), presentation switchers (IN Series), scalers (DSC, DVS), distribution amplifiers, and DSP products. Works over TCP (port 23) or RS-232 (9600 8N1).

help.overview: Universal control for Extron products using the SIS protocol. Works with 200+ products including crosspoint matrix switchers, presentation switchers, scalers, distribution amplifiers, and DSPs.
help.setup: 1. Connect the Extron device to the network or via RS-232 (9600 8N1). 2. For TCP control, set the device's IP address and use port 23 (default). 3. Extron recommends a 100ms delay between commands (pre-configured).

compatible_models.notes: Any Extron product implementing the SIS protocol (~200 products).

drivers.name: Kramer Protocol 3000
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Kramer products via Protocol 3000 over TCP (port 5000). Covers matrix switchers (VS series), scalers (VP series), distribution amplifiers, and Via wireless presentation systems.

help.overview: Controls Kramer matrix switchers, scalers, distribution amplifiers, and Via wireless presentation systems via Protocol 3000. Common in corporate AV, education, and houses of worship.
help.setup:
1. Connect the switcher to the network via Ethernet. 2. Set the IP address via the front panel menu or Kramer Network. 3. Enter the IP address and port 5000 (default) in the device config. 4. Machine number defaults to 01. Change it if multiple Kramer units
   share the same port.

drivers.name: Lightware LW3
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Lightware switchers and matrix routers via Protocol #3 (LW3) over TCP port 6107. Covers UCX, Taurus UCX, MMX2, MMX, and MX2M products. Provides video and audio crosspoint switching, mute, lock, HDCP, output 5V, embedded- audio mute, EDID switching, analog audio level/mute/balance, and CEC command sending.

help.overview: Lightware LW3 is the unified ASCII control protocol used across Lightware's matrix switchers, extenders, and modular routers. Commands target a tree of nodes (e.g. /V1/MEDIA/VIDEO/XP) using GET, SET, and CALL operations. The driver exposes the most-used runtime control surface: video and audio routing, mute, HDCP, output power, EDID, analog audio level, and CEC.
help.setup:
1. Connect the Lightware device to the network via Ethernet. 2. Confirm the device's IP address using LDC (Lightware Device Controller)
   or the front-panel display.
3. In LDC's Network tab, ensure the LW3 service on port 6107 is enabled
   and that authentication (IPLogin) is OFF — this driver does not
   authenticate.
4. Enter the IP address and port 6107 in the device config. 5. Use input/output port numbers as integers (I3 → input=3, O2 → output=2).
   Setting input=0 disconnects an output.
6. Polled state covers I1..I4 and O1..O4. Larger devices respond to
   routing commands on any valid port number.

compatible_models.notes: Any Lightware product that implements LW3 (most products since 2012). Polled state covers ports I1..I4 and O1..O4 — adequate for UCX, Taurus, and MMX2; commands accept any port number for larger MX2M frames.

drivers.name: TurtleAV Chazy Control
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls a TurtleAV Chazy Control AV-over-IP matrix controller and the sub-units it manages: video encoders (TX), decoders (RX), and video walls. The standard Control's command set; for the Media Player, Groups, Events, Scheduler, Dante Presets, Configuration Presets and Date/Time modules, use the Chazy Control Pro driver.

help.overview: The Chazy Control orchestrates a Chazy 4K AV-over-IP system. Add it as one device; its encoders, decoders and video walls appear as child entities under the Child Entities tab. For Pro-only modules (media, groups, events, schedules, presets), use the Chazy Control Pro driver instead.
help.setup:
1. Connect the controller's Control LAN to your network. The default address is 192.168.6.100; it also advertises as controller.local.
2. Telnet on port 23 is enabled by default with no login.
3. Enter the controller's IP in the device config; leave the port at 23.
4. Encoders and decoders are discovered automatically on connect from GET STATUS. Use the Search command to find new TX/RX on the Video LAN, then Add Auto All to register them.

compatible_models.notes: Adapted from the hardware-validated Control Pro driver; the standard Control API is a documented strict subset (Chazy Control API reference, FW 1.00.17). Not yet validated against a standalone Control unit.

drivers.name: TurtleAV Chazy Control Pro
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls a TurtleAV Chazy Control Pro AV-over-IP matrix controller and every sub-unit it manages: video encoders (TX) and decoders (RX), video walls, decoder groups, events, schedules, NAS/FTP media sources, Dante presets, and configuration presets.

help.overview: The Chazy Control Pro orchestrates an entire Chazy 4K AV-over-IP system. Add it as one device; its encoders, decoders, video walls, groups, events, schedules, media sources, Dante presets, and configuration presets appear as child entities under the Child Entities tab.
help.setup:
1. Connect the controller's Control LAN (LAN2) to your network. The default address is 192.168.6.100; it also advertises as controller.local.
2. Telnet on port 23 is enabled by default with no login.
3. Enter the controller's IP in the device config; leave the port at 23.
4. Encoders and decoders are discovered automatically on connect from GET STATUS. Use 'Find + Add All Devices' to search the Video LAN and enroll everything new in one step (or Search, then Add All New Devices, to do it in stages).
5. Video walls, groups, events, and Dante presets already configured on the controller are also listed automatically. Media sources, schedules, and configuration presets cannot be listed by the controller, so they appear only once you create them here.

drivers.name: TurtleAV Darwin Control
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls a TurtleAV Darwin Control (CTL100AL) H.265 AV-over-IP matrix controller and every sub-unit it manages: video encoders (TX), decoders (RX), and video walls.

help.overview: The Darwin Control orchestrates an entire Darwin HD AV-over-IP system. Add it as one device; its encoders, decoders, and video walls appear as child entities under the Child Entities tab.
help.setup:
1. Connect the controller's Control LAN (LAN2) to your network. The default address is 192.168.6.100; it also advertises as controller.local.
2. Telnet on port 23 is enabled by default with no login.
3. Enter the controller's IP in the device config; leave the port at 23.
4. Encoders and decoders are discovered automatically on connect from GET STATUS. Use the Search command to find new TX/RX on the Video LAN, then Add Auto All to register them.
5. Video walls already configured on the controller are also listed automatically.

compatible_models.notes: Verified end-to-end against live hardware (FW 1.50.02) with a live HDMI source on the TX and a display on the RX: connect, discovery, child enumeration, status parsing, enrolment/idempotency, and the operational SET surface (routing, output/mute/pause/OSD/auto, resolution, rotate, no-signal standby, HDCP/Osp SNK/SRC/OFF/H14/H22, TX encoding, LED/FPLED, audio input, IR, GPIO). OSD, mute, pause, resolution, rotation, output on/off, and a single-RX video wall tile were confirmed rendering on the attached display; the source-binding commands (video-wall class/matrix source, KVM hotkey) were accepted with a live source. Decoder video-wall mode (MODE VW) requires the RX assigned to a wall with an applied class region first. Only reboot/reset/network commands were held back on the live unit; their wire formats match the manufacturer reference. Multi-endpoint routing and multi-screen walls need additional TX/RX units to exercise.
